5 sample questions

1. In Tennessee, what is the youngest age to get a learner permit?

  1. 14 years old
  2. 15 years old (correct answer)
  3. 16 years old
  4. 17 years old

Answer: B. You can get a Tennessee learner permit at 15 after passing the written and vision tests.

Tennessee handbook, page 14.

2. In Tennessee, what is the rule on phones for drivers with a learner permit or an intermediate license?

  1. They may text only at red lights
  2. They may not use a cell phone while driving (correct answer)
  3. They may use a phone if it is on speaker
  4. They may call only family members

Answer: B. Drivers with a learner permit or an intermediate license may not use a cell phone while driving, so all their attention stays on the road.

Tennessee handbook, page 18.

3. In Tennessee, you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What does the move-over law require?

  1. Honk to warn the crew
  2. Stop completely in your lane
  3. Move to a lane farther away if safe, or else slow down (correct answer)
  4. Pass at the same speed in the next lane

Answer: C. You must move into a lane away from the stopped vehicle when it is safe; if you cannot, you must slow down as you pass.

Tennessee handbook, page 55.

4. In Tennessee, who must be in the car when a learner permit holder drives?

  1. Any passenger age 16 or older
  2. A licensed driver 18 or older in the back seat
  3. A licensed driver 21 or older in the front seat (correct answer)
  4. No one, during daylight hours

Answer: C. A learner permit holder must always have a licensed driver who is 21 or older sitting in the front seat.

Tennessee handbook, page 14.

5. In Tennessee, during which hours may a learner permit holder not drive?

  1. 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. (correct answer)
  2. Midnight to 5 a.m.
  3. 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.
  4. 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.

Answer: A. A learner permit holder may not drive between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m., even with an adult, because night driving is harder for beginners.

Tennessee handbook, page 14.
